# Verda raises $189M/€163M to accelerate development of its full-stack AI cloud and multiply compute capacity 

 Sep 22, 2026 | Jani Hellström | 3 min read 

 Verda becomes Europe's latest unicorn with $189 million in new funding. The financing includes an oversubscribed Series B led by Emergence Capital, plus additional investment. Investors participating include MUFG Innovation Partners, Supermicro, Varma Mutual Pension Insurance Company, Lifeline Ventures, ENDUR, 6 Degrees Capital (6DC), byFounders, and others. 

 The new funding allows Verda to accelerate product development across all layers of its AI cloud, from compute capacity to platform services for frontier AI teams in the agentic era.

...

## Press release 

 Helsinki, Finland — 10am EEST, Tuesday 22nd September | European technology company Verda today announced it has raised $189/€163M million in new funding to scale its full-stack AI cloud. 

 The financing includes an oversubscribed Series B led by Emergence Capital, plus additional investment. Investors participating in the financing include MUFG Innovation Partners, Supermicro, Varma Mutual Pension Insurance Company, Lifeline Ventures, ENDUR, 6 Degrees Capital (6DC), byFounders, Tesi (Finnish Industry Investment Ltd), and a group of angel investors including Ola Tørudbakken and Mark Saroufim (Core Automation and GPU MODE). 

 The new funding allows Verda to accelerate product development across all layers of its AI cloud, from compute capacity to platform services for frontier AI teams in the agentic era. Verda will invest in areas including inference, and plans to multiply its compute capacity over the next year.

...

The announcement comes after the company reached $165 million in annualized revenue run rate in July. Verda recently opened offices in London and San Francisco, and has plans for further expansion across Europe, the United States, and Asia.

...

results.title: Verda raises $189m Series B for AI cloud
highlights:
Helsinki-based AI cloud company Verda, formerly DataCrunch, has raised $189m in a Series B led by Emergence Capital. MUFG Innovation Partners, Supermicro, Varma, Lifeline Ventures, 6 Degrees Capital, byFounders, Tesi and angel investors including Ola Tørudbakken and Mark Saroufim also participated.

Verda says the financing will accelerate product development across its full-stack AI cloud and expand compute capacity. The company plans to have more than 250 MW of operations in 2027, with capacity live in Finland and further sites planned across Europe, the UK, the US and Asia. It reported reaching a $165m annualised revenue run rate in July.

## Compute capacity becomes a product constraint

Verda owns more of the stack than a software-only cloud provider, spanning data-centre capacity, GPU systems and platform services for training and inference. That can shorten the path from hardware deployment to customer workloads, but it also makes power availability, equipment delivery and utilisation central to the economics of growth.

The 250 MW target turns the Series B into an execution test. New capacity only creates value when Verda can fill it with durable workloads while controlling energy and hardware costs. Strategic participation from Supermicro may support equipment access, while the Nordic power base helps the company compete on both cost and the carbon footprint of compute.

results.title: AI cloud startup Verda raises $189m in Series B funding round - DCD
results.author: Georgia Butler
highlights:
European neocloud startup Verda has secured $189 million in a Series B funding round.

The round was led by Emergence Capital, with participation from MUFG Innovation Partners, Supermicro, Varma Mutual Pension Insurance Company, Lifeline Ventures, ENDUR, 6 Degrees Capital (6DC), byFounders, Tesi (Finnish Industry Investment Ltd), and a group of angel investors, including Ola Tørudbakken and Mark Saroufim.

 

 – Verda 

According to a company blog post announcing the fundraising, this brings Verda's total funding to more than $450 million. Previously, Verda secured $117m in an April 2026 round.

The newly injected capital will support more data center capacity coming online as well as "deeper investment in the platform." The company is targeting having more than 250MW of operational capacity by 2027.

Formerly known as DataCrunch, Verda was founded in 2020, and currently has data centers in Finland, all of which run on 100 percent renewable energy. It also operates one in Reykjanesbær in Iceland, and has further sites planned to come online across Europe, the UK, the US, and Asia. In September detailed plans for a data center project in the Hanhela area of ​​Pyhäjoki municipality in Finland.

The company secured $64.6 million in a Series A funding round in September 2025, at the time noting it was planning an AI data center in Latvia. Prior to that, in an October 2024 seed funding round, the company raised $13m.

...

In addition to increasing its data center footprint, Verda is also planning to deploy the Nvidia Vera Rubin NVL72 systems in the coming months. In terms of its platform, Verda is also "on the path to release S3-compatible Object Storage."

In April 2026, Verda said it would offer customers access to Arm's AGI CPU that was developed in conjunction with Meta. The AGI CPU would work alongside Nvidia GB300 racks. Built on TSMC’s 3nm process node, the AGI CPU comprises 136 Arm Neoverse V3 cores running up to 3.7GHz.

results.title: Finnish AI cloud startup Verda raises $189 million Series B, crossing $1 billion valuation
results.author: Hugo Rojas
highlights:
Verda, the Helsinki-based AI cloud company formerly known as DataCrunch, closed a $189 million Series B on September 22, 2026, lifting its valuation past $1 billion. The company said it is valued at at least $1 billion after the round, which was led by Emergence Capital, declining to disclose an exact valuation.

...

The €164.8 million ($189 million) financing brings Verda’s total funding to over $450 million across equity and debt, according to the company. That makes it one of the largest single rounds ever raised by a European AI infrastructure company in this funding cycle.

...

Verda raised a $13 million seed round in 2024 and a $64 million Series A in 2025. In April 2026, Verda announced another $117 million equity-and-debt package, later expanded to $155 million with financing from Nordic Investment Bank. 

The September Series B nearly doubles that previous tranche in a single close, reflecting the accelerating pace of capital deployment in the AI infrastructure sector, a dynamic also evident in the GPU factory qualification push that has gripped the industry this year.

 Verda now powers AI workloads for organizations across more than 50 countries, ranging from early-stage startups to enterprises, and reached a $165 million annualized revenue run rate as of July 2026, with a team of more than 250 people spread across Helsinki, London, Taipei and San Francisco.

...

The new capital will help Verda scale the layers of the stack that cutting-edge AI teams rely on for growth, expanding physical compute capacity while building out platform services and tools for the agentic era. 

 Verda must secure accelerators, data centers, networking equipment and power before customers can consume the resulting capacity, meaning software margins may arrive later while the hardware bill arrives first.

...

The financing, reported by Bloomberg on September 22, underscores continued investor appetite for the infrastructure powering the artificial intelligence boom. Verda has raised over €392.3 million ($450 million) in total funding and gains a runway to build out data center footprint across Europe at a time when sovereign AI ambitions and data-residency requirements are nudging enterprise buyers toward regional alternatives.

Whether Verda can convert its self-reported revenue run rate into durable, high-utilization demand will determine how far its unicorn valuation holds as the GPU supply glut debate intensifies across the sector.

results.title: Verda, nuvem de IA da Finlândia, levanta US$ 189 milhões e vira unicórnio
results.author: Gustavo Bonato Abrão
highlights:
[ TL;DR ] 

- Série B de US$ 189 milhões (cerca de R$ 970 milhões) liderada pela Emergence Capital; total captado passa de US$ 450 milhões entre capital e dívida
- A empresa se diz avaliada em pelo menos US$ 1 bilhão, mas recusou revelar o valor exato à Bloomberg
- Receita anualizada saltou de US$ 60 milhões em abril para US$ 165 milhões em julho, segundo a própria Verda, sem balanço auditado
- Fundada numa garagem de Helsinque em 2020 como DataCrunch, trocou de nome em novembro de 2025
- Tabela de preços é pública: H100 a US$ 3,37 por hora e B200 a US$ 6,55, com spot pela metade

A Verda, nuvem de computação para IA sediada em Helsinque, levantou US$ 189 milhões (cerca de R$ 970 milhões na cotação de hoje, sem impostos brasileiros) numa Série B liderada pela Emergence Capital e passou a dizer que vale pelo menos US$ 1 bilhão. O valor exato da avaliação ficou fora do anúncio.

Ruben Bryon, engenheiro belga, montou o primeiro rack de GPUs da empresa numa garagem em Helsinque, em 2020, e a operação passou a se pagar em poucas semanas. Seis anos depois, a mesma empresa soma mais de US$ 450 milhões captados entre capital e dívida, o equivalente a R$ 2,3 bilhões.

...

Segundo a Bloomberg, a empresa se recusou a revelar quanto vale acima do bilhão. A Emergence Capital, que liderou, investiu cedo em Salesforce e Zoom e costuma apostar em software corporativo, não em Data Centers cheios de GPU.

...

## De DataCrunch a Verda em seis anos

1. 2020

#### Garagem em Helsinque

Bryon lança uma nuvem de GPU autoatendida com o nome DataCrunch. Operação no azul em semanas.
2. 2024

#### Seed de US$ 13 milhões

Primeira rodada institucional, depois de cerca de 300 reuniões com investidores que achavam o negócio caro demais.
3. Set/Nov 2025

#### Série A e novo nome

US$ 64 milhões, selo de parceira preferencial da NVIDIA e a troca de DataCrunch para Verda.
4. Abr 2026

#### US$ 117 milhões em capital e dívida

Rodada liderada pela Lifeline Ventures, ampliada para US$ 155 milhões com o Nordic Investment Bank.
5. 22 set 2026

#### Série B de US$ 189 milhões

Emergence Capital lidera. Empresa se declara unicórnio.

O nome atual chegou em novembro de 2025, junto com a Série A de US$ 64 milhões e o selo de parceira preferencial da NVIDIA. A empresa explica Verda como junção do espanhol para "verdadeiro" com o esperanto para "verde". A troca coincidiu com a guinada de discurso para soberania de dados e nuvem fora do alcance da lei americana Cloud Act.

A receita anualizada é o número que sustenta o unicórnio, e ele vem da própria empresa. Eram mais de US$ 60 milhões em abril, US$ 100 milhões no fim do primeiro semestre e US$ 165 milhões (R$ 845 milhões) em julho. Nenhum balanço auditado acompanha o anúncio, e receita anualizada pega o mês mais recente e multiplica por doze.

...

As duas fecharam o período com prejuízo líquido, enquanto a Verda diz operar no azul desde a garagem.

...

Inferência é a prioridade declarada, ou seja, o serviço de rodar modelos já treinados para responder usuários e agentes, em vez de treinar do zero. A empresa também promete multiplicar a capacidade de computação em um ano e chegar a mais de 250 MW de operação em 2027, com Data Centers hoje só na Finlândia e novos na Europa, no Reino Unido, nos EUA e na Ásia.

...

> A demanda por computação de IA é insaciável, e a distância para a oferta só cresce.

## Quanto custa uma hora de GPU na Verda

| GPU (1 unidade) | VRAM | Sob demanda | Spot |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GB300 SXM6 | 288 GB | US$ 9,16/h | US$ 4,58/h |
| B300 SXM6 | 268 GB | US$ 7,96/h | US$ 3,98/h |
| B200 SXM6 | 180 GB | US$ 6,55/h | US$ 3,27/h |
| H200 SXM5 | 141 GB | US$ 4,41/h | US$ 2,21/h |
| H100 SXM5 | 80 GB | US$ 3,37/h | US$ 1,68/h |
| A100 SXM4 | 80 GB | US$ 1,74/h | US$ 0,87/h |

A tabela é pública e em dólar, sem pedir orçamento. A hora de uma H100 sai por US$ 3,37 (cerca de R$ 17) sob demanda, e o preço spot, que pode ser interrompido a qualquer momento, corta tudo pela metade. A empresa se diz até 90% mais barata que AWS, Azure e Google Cloud, e a comparação depende de qual instância e de qual desconto se usa na outra ponta.

Contrato de dois anos rende 25% de desconto sobre a tabela, e clusters com InfiniBand de até 144 GPUs saem no autoatendimento, sem falar com vendedor. Os dados ficam em Data Centers finlandeses que a empresa diz rodar com energia 100% renovável.

...

Tudo o mais está publicado. A tabela de preços, o desconto por contrato longo, o cadastro sem conversa com vendedor e o status de parceira preferencial da NVIDIA aparecem no site, e qualquer um confere em dois minutos.

Uma equipe brasileira abre conta hoje, sobe um contêiner e paga por hora numa B200 de 180 GB, US$ 6,55 (uns R$ 34), sem contrato de meses nem fila de aprovação. Para quem não tem gerente de conta em Seattle, esse acesso direto já funciona, com a tabela de setembro de 2026 e as GPUs que a NVIDIA lançou este ano.

results.title: ClusterMAX 3.0: The Industry Standard GPU Cloud Rating ...
results.author: Jordan Nanos, Sam Harshe, Samuel Kruse, Pratt Bhatt, Billy Cao
highlights:
In 8 months since our last major release of ClusterMAX, slavering investors have just about run out of pockets to stuff checks into. GPU supply has gone to zero. Meanwhile, we have been hard at work putting clusters through the ringer.

...

- ClusterMAX 3.0 debuts with a comprehensive review of the neocloud industry, covering 77 providers.
- We increase our market view to cover 323 providers, up from 209 in ClusterMAX 2.0, 169 in ClusterMAX 1.0, and 124 in the original AI Neocloud Playbook and Anatomy article.
- We have now interviewed well over 200 end users of neoclouds as part of this research.
- We update our itemized list of criteria across 10 categories, and update our direct descriptions of our expectations for Slurm, Kubernetes, Standalone Machines, Monitoring Dashboards, and Health Checks. All of this content is live on our website. We encourage providers to use these lists when developing their offerings. We still consider these lists as an amalgamation of our experience interviewing end users, making them representative of the features that end users expect from their cloud providers.
- Nebius joins CoreWeave in the Platinum tier. While CoreWeave still sets the technical bar for others to follow, Nebius is now established as a provider that consistently commands a premium pricing over others. Strong business decisions by Nebius have put them in a position to serve an entire class of neolabs at seller’s prices.
- Google Cloud joins Oracle in the Gold tier. Azure moves to Silver, Fluidstack moves to Unavailable, and Crusoe drops to Bronze. Lambda, Firmus and TensorWave remain in Silver, while GMI moves up to Silver from Bronze.
- Many companies drop from Silver (or Gold) to Bronze or lower. We raise the bar this round as only 19 neoclouds globally achieve a Medallion rating.
- We establish a tier between Bronze and Underperforming: the Participation Ribbon tier. 15 providers join this rating, which more accurately describes our opinion that they do the bare minimum to get by.

...

Meanwhile, lenders also need evidence that a provider can deliver its cluster on time and meet the SLAs in their customer contract. ... This has led multiple insurance providers to enter the market with parametric offerings that protect neoclouds and their lenders against contract terminations, typically offering a one-month bridge to find a new offtaker in the event of a termination. We are big fans of this structure, and believe it to be a solid method for lenders to use to de-risk these transactions.

results.title: Verda AI Cloud Startup Secures $189 Million in Funding Round | AInvest
results.author: Beyond the Headlines
highlights:
- Helsinki-based Verda secured $189M in funding, boosting total capital past $450M to compete in AI cloud computing.

- The firm claims profitability with $100M annual revenue, leveraging Finland's renewable energy and 90% lower pricing vs. AWS/Azure.

- Expansion risks diluting its cost advantage as U.S./Asia operations face higher energy costs and competition from CoreWeave/Lambda.

...

Helsinki-based Verda, the GPU-cloud company formerly known as DataCrunch, said on September 22, 2026 that it had raised an additional $189 million, lifting its cumulative funding past $450 million. Verda sells on-demand Nvidia NVDA-- compute to AI teams — the same business that the public company CoreWeave CRWV-- is racing to scale against the budgets of Amazon AMZN--, Microsoft MSFT--, and Google GOOGL--. A headline about a young company's fresh capital reads as momentum. The first thing worth checking is what, if anything, an ordinary investor can do with it.

...

The $189 million is also not Verda's first round. In April it announced a $117 million round led by the Finnish venture firm Lifeline Ventures, with participation from byFounders, Tesi, and Varma plus debt from a group of Nordic financial institutions. The company adopted the name Verda late in 2025, after a roughly €55 million Series A, under its earlier identity as DataCrunch.

...

What sets the company apart in this round of headlines is a single word: profitable. Most AI-infrastructure vendors spend ahead of revenue on chips and capacity. Verda says it is cash flow positive, with revenue that doubled to more than $60 million in the first quarter of 2026 and reached a $100 million annual run rate by June, having grown tenfold in eighteen months.

The source of that edge is geographic. Verda's data centers sit in Finland, run on 100% renewable energy, and use natural cooling, which keeps power costs low; because it owns the servers, networking, and software itself rather than reselling rented capacity, it claims pricing up to 90% below what Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud charge. Being one of a small group of Nvidia "Preferred Partners" is meant to secure earlier access to scarce chips. Its customers include Nokia NOK--, 1X, ExpressVPN, and Freepik.

Three things should keep that claim from being taken at face value. First, "profitable" is the company's own description, not an audited result, and it arrives at small scale — a $100 million run rate against a CoreWeave measured in billions. Profitability at that size does not prove profitability at scale.

Second, the cheap-power advantage is exactly the part that does not travel. Finland supplies low-cost renewable electricity and free natural cooling; expanding into the United States and Asia, as Verda says it plans, removes both and places it head-on against CoreWeave and Lambda, which already hold capacity and customers in those regions. The model that works in Helsinki is not guaranteed to work in Virginia or Singapore.

Third, the round's size is itself a reminder of how much capital this business consumes. Much of Verda's funding has come as debt from Nordic financial institutions, and GPUs are expensive no matter the power bill. Raising money accumulates that weight rather than removing it.

Stripped of momentum, the round carries one practical lesson for a retail investor. There is no Verda share to buy today — the company has disclosed no IPO plans, so the outcome is not directly ownable. What the round does validate is a competitive signal: a low-cost, cash-flow-positive entrant that undercuts hyperscalers on price, if its model survives the move outside Finland, is pressure on the margins and capital-intensity assumptions priced into the public AI-compute names.
